characters.Melchior Aebischer: Deceased; found dead at the Chrachen gorge near Lauenegg. Husband of Berta. Chin scar (axe). Heavily in debt (innkeeper, Rutz, everyone). Known drunk on the Chrachenpfad. Official cause: heart failure during a ~12m fall. Found face-down between two boulders, nailed boots.
characters.Dr. Konrad Stettler: Amtsarzt (district physician), 58. Examines the body, rules 'Herzversagen, vermutlich beim Sturz.' Delivers the death certificate, argues against an autopsy on cost/predictability grounds.
characters.Martin Feuz: Untersuchungsrichter (investigating judge), young. Methodical note-taker (double-underlines). Interviews witnesses; accepts no-autopsy; files the certificate in his oak cabinet.
characters.Berta Aebischer: Widow of Melchior. Identifies the body by the chin scar; keeps gloves on. Last saw him the previous evening. Hesitates a beat too long before agreeing with Stettler's account.
characters.Marolf: Young Träger of the Dorfwehr who retrieves the body. Dialect speaker; notes Melchior's debts and unsteadiness.
characters.Rutz: [⚠️ WRONG — canonized from a Writer slip] Recorded as a local creditor to whom Melchior owed money; waits silently in the hallway to hear the matter is settled. (Canon per Phase 3: Rutz is the village PRIEST and Stettler's old friend/confessor.)

locations.Der Chrachen: Gorge south of Lauenegg; stream freezes greenish in winter. Site of Melchior's fatal ~12m fall. Includes the treacherous Chrachenpfad.
locations.Lauenegg: The village; the Chrachen lies to its south.
locations.Amtsraum (unheated examination room): Unheated official room where the body is laid out under a too-short sheet for identification.
locations.Feuz's Amtsstube: The judge's office with an oak filing cabinet; adjoining hallway where Rutz waits.

objects.Der Totenschein: Death certificate by Stettler recording heart failure during the fall; filed without autopsy.
objects.Narbe am Kinn: Melchior's chin scar (old axe injury); used by Berta to identify him.
objects.Genagelte Bergschuhe: Melchior's nailed mountain boots, protruding from under the sheet.
objects.Eichenschrank: Oak cabinet in Feuz's office where the certificate is filed.

timeline.description: Night: snow; Melchior falls to his death in the Chrachen (~12m).
By first light: the Dorfwehr (incl. Marolf) retrieves the body.
Morning: Stettler examines the body, declares heart failure/fall; Feuz interviews witnesses on site.
Same day: body moved to the Amtsraum; Berta identifies and is questioned.
Afternoon: Stettler delivers the certificate; Feuz declines autopsy and files it; Rutz waits in the hallway.

foreshadowing: Berta hesitates a beat too long before agreeing with Stettler's account.
Accidental-death verdict accepted for cost/convenience despite an incomplete exam — possible cover-up.
Melchior's debts establish financial motives for multiple parties.
Rutz waits to hear the matter is 'settled' — a personal stake.
Berta's 'dass er einmal hinunterfällt' reads as ominous foreknowledge.
Feuz double-underlines notes — privately flagged something while closing the case.
